artists.biography:
Mazzy Star is an American alternative rock band formed in Santa Monica, California, in 1989 from the group Opal, a collaboration of guitarist David Roback and bassist Kendra Smith. Roback's friend Hope Sandoval became the group's vocalist when Smith left the band.

Mazzy Star is probably best known for the song "Fade into You" which brought the band some success in the mid-1990s and was the group's biggest mainstream hit, earning extensive exposure on MTV, VH1, and radio airplay. Roback and Sandoval are the creative center of the band, with Sandoval as lyricist and Roback as composer of the majority of the band's material.

perplexity.description:
Ghost Highway is a live compilation album by Mazzy Star, capturing performances from 1994 during the band's peak period. The album comprises two distinct sessions: eight tracks recorded at The Metro in Chicago in November 1994, and five tracks from a KROQ radio broadcast in Los Angeles from the same year. These recordings showcase the band's alternative and psychedelic rock sound during a formative moment in their career, just as their breakthrough album So Tonight I Might See was gaining commercial traction.

The album features material spanning Mazzy Star's catalog, including songs that would become central to their identity. "Ghost Highway," the title track, originated from the band's earlier incarnation as Opal and represents a faster, more psychedelic-driven composition compared to the dreamy aesthetic they would later become known for. The setlist demonstrates the band's range, blending their signature melancholic alternative rock with covers and deeper cuts that reveal their musical influences and evolution.

As a live release, Ghost Highway serves primarily as a historical document rather than a commercial statement, preserving performances from a pivotal moment before Mazzy Star achieved wider recognition. The album was eventually released in 2015 as a CD-only edition, making these 1994 recordings available to fans decades after they were captured. It remains a valuable artifact for understanding the band's live presence and sonic approach during the mid-1990s.
